brief: Morgan Stanley argues that political opposition to data centers, not weak demand or scarce capital, is the live risk to the AI capex cycle. The opposition is broad and cross-party. A Gallup poll shows seven in ten Americans oppose local data-center construction, with roughly two-thirds of Republicans, nearly 80% of independents and 83% of Democrats opposed. It is converting into policy: New York's July state-level pause, a Texas review that also paused new approvals and grid connections, roughly 500 jurisdictions with bans or moratoriums and 14 more states considering them, plus ~$156 billion of projects cancelled or delayed in 2025 and ~$130 billion affected in 1Q26. The stake is large because MS economists put AI investment at 0.6pp of 2025 real GDP growth, 0.8pp in 1H26 and 0.85pp of a forecast 2.6% in 2027, so deferral weighs on growth directly and through the wealth effect on consumption. Because the constraint is regulatory rather than demand, the note reads the scenario as raising scarcity value for hyperscalers, negative for AI adopters, and, via lower issuance, potentially spread-tightening for credit. A slowdown is not the base case.
